title: Larkhollow
dek: A remote settlement with a Petal Market, a dangerous tower and forest roads whose changing routes draw adventurers back with new questions.
sources: Quest-RP continuation — supplied 11 Oct 2026; 2,369 messages, main quest-rp and Pristinia Library; posting dates, not in-world dates
Larkhollow_Deep_Location_Dossier.md · existing chronology retained; travel limits checked against narrator posts
Quest RP refreshed source · supplied 23 October 2026 · 3,845 messages across the main channel and two accessible threads; posting chronology and narrated continuations remain distinct
body:
Larkhollow is much newer to the recorded adventuring history than Pristinia, Gael, or The Before. Its account separates what existed before contact from what adventurers have learned since arriving. The settlement lies far enough from established centers that reaching it requires meaningful travel, and a ruined tower already gives the place a visible history older than the visiting parties.

29 June 2026 · first recovered arrival

Travelers reach Larkhollow and find lodging with a view toward the ruined tower. At the expedition’s end, the location opens for continued roleplay, turning a destination on one journey into a place characters can revisit and inhabit socially. This is the beginning of Larkhollow’s player-facing history, not the beginning of the settlement itself.

The ruined tower

By 28 July, characters refer to relics associated with the old tower. The record confirms that the ruin has material remains and local significance without yet establishing who built it, why it fell, or what the settlement’s people believe happened there.

A destination on the wider travel network

By 7 September, another company prepares to travel from the coast of Gael through Verdelune toward Larkhollow, a journey described as taking many hours. The settlement is no longer merely the endpoint of one quest. It is a recognized destination with a repeatable route.

Current state and open record

Larkhollow is reachable, inhabitable, and only lightly explored. The tower’s builders and destruction, the settlement’s economy and political relationships, the dangers along its routes, and the effect of regular adventurer traffic remain open. Its history should be allowed to accumulate rather than being completed in advance.

September–October · a market and an unsettled forest

The continuation gives Larkhollow a center of ordinary trade: the Petal Market, with herbalist Sylvi Fernstep, Ilyra Bellflower, trinket collector Orin Mossbell and carpet vendor Talla Briarwing. These are witnessed local roles; their authority and complete histories are not established.

The route through Verdelune becomes less predictable. Hana’s tower turns a September visit into a retreat, and Ilyra’s later letter directs an expedition to Viota’s monument. Larkhollow is now a place to question residents and return to with new evidence. The tower’s purpose, the forest’s changing time and the first passage remain open.

Scene sources: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Knowing the route is not making it safe

At the end of the recovered June arrival, the narrator permits rest and continuing roleplay while explicitly warning that travel there is not yet safe. September’s company stages from Gael for the onward journey through Verdelune; its discussion of the long trip is travel knowledge, not a fixed timetable or a guarantee of passage.

Later market and forest encounters remain part of the settlement’s developing record. The earlier dossier’s description of a lightly explored destination does not erase those subsequent events. Neither first adventurer contact nor a known route establishes the settlement’s founding, its political ruler, or the origin of every relic near its tower.

The forest beyond the river

The later Selwyn expedition crosses the river near the mountains into the dark forest leading toward Larkhollow. The narrator calls the immediate encounter area the Dark Shroud. There the company fights childlike figures around a rooted body; Fenwick’s meteor spell ignites trees.

The source establishes damage at that encounter, not destruction of all Larkhollow or the entire forest. The eventual release of the body depends on Minerva remaining with the figures. Their claims about living trees and transformation remain attributed.

Scene references: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
